title: A command script
description:
Run simple script files that a mod can ship, without giving them access to everything.

```
spawn goblin 5 3
give player potion 2
say "Welcome to the arena!"
-> 3 commands run; "teleport" is not allowed for mods -> refused at line 4
```
hints: `<sstream>` gives streams over strings. `std::istringstream in{ text };` reads from a string exactly like `std::cin` (`in >> word >> number`, or `std::getline(in, line)` for one line at a time), and its condition is false once a read fails. `std::ostringstream out; out << "x " << 5; out.str()` builds a string the way `std::cout` prints.
`std::quoted` reads a quoted string from a stream: `stream >> std::quoted(word)` (lesson 13.02).
The command table is the security boundary: mods can only do what is in it.
requirements: One command per line; arguments split on spaces, with quoted strings kept together.
A table of allowed commands with the number of arguments each takes.
Report the line number of any error and keep running the rest.
stretch: Add `if` and variables, and see how fast a "simple" script language grows.
